scope: Period airspeed correction audit for British, German and captured Japanese WW2 fighter stall observations; retains original speed basis and prohibits extrapolation.

ingestion_policy.principle: CAS* is provisional and permitted only when the actual measured IAS has an independently documented instrument calibration and installation/position correction (or a primary source's combined IAS-to-correct-indicated mapping) from a matched aircraft, pitot-static system, flap/gear configuration, valid speed domain and power/sideslip regime.
ingestion_policy.interpolation: Only between original numerical points from a matched, monotonic, in-range calibration series. If corrections are specified as discrete intervals, honor interval boundaries separately; do not interpolate across a jump. No extrapolation below the first original speed or above the last.
ingestion_policy.instrument_position_separation: If the original report gives water-column airspeed and position correction, apply the instrument correction first; do not add position correction directly to cockpit IAS. Use the source's final calibrated speed when provided.
ingestion_policy.speed_labels: Keep original report's explicit IAS, indicated, calibrated and correct-indicated nomenclature. NACA 'correct indicated' is not an authority to silently relabel separately reported 'indicated' stall points without checking which instrument the plot/record used.
ingestion_policy.variant_guard: No borrowed PEC from Spitfire VA to IX/XVI, Hurricane II Z2963 to another Hurricane, Bf109 E to F/G, Fw190 A3 to A4/D9, or A6M3 EB-201 to A6M2/A6M5 unless original equipment and installation are documented identical and cross-checked.

rejected_cas_conversions.reason: No original PEC below 120mph IAS; cannot extrapolate +4 mph interval to stall; VA NACA data is wrong variant.
Pilot-note PEC at 100mph and above; no documented correction for IAS60–80. NACA Hurricane II has different variant/airframe.
Pilot-note PEC starts 100mph; Z2963 NACA calibration cannot be silently transferred to other Hurricane II airframes; original OCR 60-90 versus 80-90 unresolved.
Instrument and PEC components available only for IAS>=120, so both power-off stalls remain IAS.
Report's PEC measurements were with gear/flaps up at speed range used for high-speed test; no independently verified low-speed points near IAS75–85 and cannot apply to gear/flaps down.
Original trailing-head method documented, but cockpit-75 versus trailing-head-95.5 claim currently only secondhand and meaning of TAS/IAS/CAS not verified against original numerical table.
Separate Fw190 EB104 calibration exists, but source says neither A3 RAF nor A4 USAAF PEC reaches exact stall 110 mph IAS; forum's assumed 100–106mph CAS is an extrapolation, reject.
112/102 IAS measured, no matched numerical low-speed PEC; Bf109E trailing-head data cannot transfer.
Original 102/90/79 mph IAS test points but no matched numerical instrument + position correction at IAS79–102 established.

pending_source_leads.target: Locate original Fig3 position error plot; confirm minimum speed axis and cockpit instrument/calibration provenance. Original transcript Table III only has ~276–398 mph IAS.

Digitize Fig7 independently for separate flap-up and flap-down flight configurations; trace whether NACA stall table 'indicated' already comes from calibrated right-wingtip recorder before correction, to avoid double correction.
Digitize Fig5 independently for cruise, glide and landing; use only VA data and match source signal before applying to stalls.
Original RAF A3 low-speed PEC numerical measurement and verify Fw190 EB104 Fig1 range. Any below-stall extension requires fresh original test data, not forum extrapolation.
Recover original 60-foot trailing-head versus cockpit IAS stall paired numerical data, including static corrections and actual test weight.
Recover original facsimile and inspect 160mph transcription inconsistency (159.5 + 4.5 != 164.8).

bottom_line: No existing RAF Spitfire IX/Hurricane I/II pilot-note, A6M3 Hamp EB201, Tempest V, Fw190 A3, Bf109 G2 or Ki84 stall IAS may be converted to CAS solely using the currently authenticated above-stall-speed PEC tables. Original NACA near-stall cockpit curves for Spitfire VA and Hurricane II are genuine new primary leads; direct NACA Hurricane II 7014lb 8-point measured stall series is captured. The numerical conversions remain gated on source-specific graph digitization and measured instrument provenance.
